title: Sixteenth stale-suite triage draw, filed under P3 item 26: ranks 1-20 of the verdict-aware ranking, 20 directories, 20 drawn files, each executed, verdicts only
idNote: Recorded under the standing P3 item 26 rather than a new T id: T-400..T-599 and T-700..T-799 are exhausted and the T-800+ range is an owner decision. Precedent: item 26 draws 7 and 15.

scope.drawnFrom: governedRiskRanking ranks 1-20 of docs/architecture/test-ci-coverage-census.json on the base, first drawable path of each directory. 0 critical and 0 high remain, so all 20 are band unclassified.
scope.everyFileWasExecuted: Each file was run on its own with npx jest --runTestsByPath <file> --no-coverage --ci --json on the base. Counts are what jest reported, never read from the census.
scope.reachability: Every subject was resolved from the test's imports and checked against docs/architecture/unreachable-components.json (orphans) and docs/architecture/orphaned-lib-modules.json (testOnly, unreferenced). Each wiring row's subject was also confirmed imported by a non-test file.
scope.liveCorpus: Seven rows read tenant data through process.cwd(). Five are red because the tenant registry was narrowed to two active tenants on 2026-08-16 or because a legacy dataset root was deleted on 2026-07-13; two are green but pin counts over the live intake. None is wired by this draw: wiring an exact count over a corpus that is being rebuilt makes a gate that fails when the data improves.
scope.readOnly: No workflow, baseline or test file is changed by this record. The census is regenerated so the 20 files are held out of the next draw with their verdicts published.

secondHalf.what: Wire the 7 wire_into_ci rows, each re-executed on the then-current main first. The 5 repair rows and 2 held_unwired rows wait on one data-lane decision (frozen fixture, registry-pinned expectation, or retirement). The ledger migration-text case is decided before rank 12 is wired. The five T-775 rows stay held until their owner acts.

suites.rationale: Green 2 of 2, behavioural, reads no repository file. Subject src/lib/dependencies is imported by the /api/dependencies routes and listed in neither reachability registry.

Green 8 of 8, behavioural, reads no repository file. Subject src/lib/email/send.ts is imported by src/lib/notifications/dispatch.ts and src/lib/programs/approval-notifications.ts, and listed in neither registry.

Red 5 of 7. The cases pin six active tenants and per-tenant row counts from before the tenant registry was narrowed to two active tenants (ca47ed85eb, 2026-08-16); the build now processes 2. Reads the live tenant corpus through process.cwd(). Repair is owed, and which repair is a data-lane call: re-pin the expectation to the registry as it now stands (two active tenants), rebuild the case on a frozen fixture so the gate cannot invert when the corpus changes, or retire the builder. Not repaired and not wired here.

Green 4 of 4, behavioural, reads no repository file. Subject layer3-validation.ts is imported by scripts/data-build/refresh-runtime-layers.ts; mapping-profiles.ts by the CSV source adapter. Neither is in a reachability registry.

Red 1 of 8. The case expects the audit to list F05_applications-systems.csv, a file under a legacy dataset root deleted by 4a7ebcd854 (2026-07-13) under the registry policy legacyDatasetRootsAreDeletedFromRepo. The behaviour is correct; the expectation names a file that no longer exists. Repair is owed, and which repair is a data-lane call: re-pin the expectation to the registry as it now stands (two active tenants), rebuild the case on a frozen fixture so the gate cannot invert when the corpus changes, or retire the builder. Not repaired and not wired here.

Red 1 of 2. The case pins five expected tenants; the registry has declared two active tenants since ca47ed85eb (2026-08-16). Reads the live tenant corpus. Repair is owed, and which repair is a data-lane call: re-pin the expectation to the registry as it now stands (two active tenants), rebuild the case on a frozen fixture so the gate cannot invert when the corpus changes, or retire the builder. Not repaired and not wired here.

Red 15 of 27. The cases iterate a hard-coded tenant list that treats four tenants as active; the registry has listed all four as retired since ca47ed85eb (2026-08-16), so the serving layer correctly returns no context for them. Repair is owed, and which repair is a data-lane call: re-pin the expectation to the registry as it now stands (two active tenants), rebuild the case on a frozen fixture so the gate cannot invert when the corpus changes, or retire the builder. Not repaired and not wired here.

Red 5 of 5, every case ENOENT. The SUBJECT, not the test, hard-codes a file under a legacy dataset root deleted by 4a7ebcd854 (2026-07-13). The admin data-layer explorer reads only the generated latest report (readLatestSkyHarborApplicationsRegeneration), so no product route reaches the broken read; the builder script scripts/audit/build-skyharbor-applications-candidate.ts does, and cannot run. Repair is owed, and which repair is a data-lane call: re-pin the expectation to the registry as it now stands (two active tenants), rebuild the case on a frozen fixture so the gate cannot invert when the corpus changes, or retire the builder. Not repaired and not wired here.

Green 4 of 4, but the subject builds from the live tenant intake under datasets/tenant-inputs/active/meridian-health/current, which is being rebuilt. Wired as is, its exact counts (sourceFiles toHaveLength(6)) make a gate that goes red when the corpus improves. Held until the same data-lane decision as the repair rows: frozen fixture or registry-pinned expectation.

Green 3 of 3, but it reads the live tenant intake under datasets/tenant-inputs/active/meridian-health/current through process.cwd(). Same hold as rank 9.
